claim: Drift aggregates: with TWO gates drifted at once (one hand-edited, one removed after a criteria-pinned pass), both runtimes report both — doctor emits one problem line PER gate in the same sorted order with per-line bytes twin-identical and exit 1; both sweeps annotate BOTH gates and add 2 to the failing count; the node sweep's annotated set equals exactly the set doctor/`hb.js drift` computes (no plumbing drop between the walk and the sweep); both ticks wake criteria_drift with count=2; and when exclusion leaves ZERO evaluable gates the sweep still exits 1 with the drift annotation, never a vacuous '✅ ALL GATES PASS' over 0 re-verified gates.
violation: On a two-drifted-gate fixture: a doctor lists only one gate or the runtimes order/word the lines differently; a sweep annotates one gate or adds only 1 to the failing count; the sweep's annotated set differs from doctor's drifted set on the same fixture; a tick reports count=1 or the counts diverge across runtimes; or a fixture whose every ever-pinned gate is drifted makes gate.sh --all (or hb gate --all) print the all-green verdict / exit 0.

claim: The drift walk is total and runtime-agreed on hostile logs: for any events.jsonl/dag.json pair containing degenerate shapes — gate_passed with criteria:[] or a non-list criteria value (never a pin), pin criteria entries missing id or cmd, dag criteria entries with null or missing id, duplicated pin events, gate_regated/gate_rearmed for gates never pinned or absent from the dag, and an ever-pinned gate whose dag entry survives but whose criteria key is removed, nulled, or emptied (emptying IS drift) — both doctors terminate without a traceback/stack and agree byte-for-byte on drift membership and exit code.
violation: Either runtime raises/stack-traces on such a log, or the two runtimes classify the same log+dag differently — e.g. a pin criterion missing 'id' compared against a dag criterion with "id": null, where node stringifies undefined/null ('undefined' vs 'null') while python maps both to 'None', flipping drift on one runtime only; or emptying an ever-pinned gate's criteria array stays quiet on either runtime.

claim: Parking silences neither the doctor nor the tick, and drift outranks dispatch under the DEFAULT environment: with the drifted gate's phase parked, doctor still exits 1 naming the gate and the tick still wakes criteria_drift on both runtimes; with an unparked dispatchable task ready, the tick wakes criteria_drift instead of handing out work; and all of this holds with HB_ROT_CHECK absent from the environment (the default-'1' path in both runtimes), not only when a test exports HB_ROT_CHECK=1.
violation: Parking the drifted phase drops the doctor problem or the tick wake on either runtime; a tick on a drifted project with ready work returns next_task (dispatches over live drift); or unsetting HB_ROT_CHECK makes the criteria_drift wake disappear on either runtime.

claim: Every advisory surface beyond the four protocol tables names criteria_drift as a human-needed stop with the regate-cycle cure and no self-sanction path: the regenerated PROTOCOL.md (hb protocol --md / bootstrap's .hb/PROTOCOL.md) carries the criteria_drift row matching the hb.js table; `hb protocol criteria_drift` answers on both runtimes; heartbeat-detect.sh's emitted hook text lists criteria_drift in BOTH its keep-looping-until list and its when-blocked diagnose list; mcp_server.py's tick tool description lists it among the loop-stopping reasons; and SKILL.md's reason-table row exists, names the full regate cycle (declare, different-actor rearm with evidence, fresh pass; git-restore to retract), and forbids freezing or editing past it.
violation: The rendered PROTOCOL.md lacks the criteria_drift row or diverges from the hb.js table; `hb protocol criteria_drift` errors or returns empty on either runtime; the hook text or the mcp tick description omits criteria_drift from its stop list; the SKILL.md row is missing; or any of these surfaces' text offers --freeze, tick --freeze, or an auto-fix as the response to criteria_drift.

claim: The duplicate-phase-id lint rule is an ERROR with cross-runtime identity and full generality: any dag with a repeated phase id — a pre-existing (non-appended) pair, or three-plus copies — is rejected by BOTH lints with the identical finding text 'duplicate phase ID: <id>' as an error (never a warning), duplicate-free plans never trip it, and the two lints return identical results (per the parity contract on `lint`) on degenerate phase objects too — a phase lacking an 'id' key must yield the same lint outcome on both runtimes, not a python traceback (p["id"] KeyError) against a clean node report.
violation: One runtime errors while the other warns or accepts; the finding texts differ; a duplicate sitting outside the appended region (or a triple) escapes either lint; a valid plan is rejected by the new rule; or an id-less phase crashes py lint with a traceback while node lint returns a normal result.

claim: The dedup/flake re-specs keep their original teeth and are drift-clean by construction: at the moment each re-specified assertion sweeps (T160.3/.4, T161.1-.2, py test_all_dedup_respects_timeout_and_failure and test_sweep_flake_probe_labels_but_never_absolves), the fixture's drift walk is EMPTY on the relevant runtime — the gates under test are genuinely re-evaluated, never satisfied vacuously via the drift exclusion — because the staged regressions flip BEHAVIOR (flag files) while criteria bytes stay pinned by a prior arming pass; and the originally proven properties still bind with falsifying force: a shared cached failure executes once (+1 flake probe) yet fails every referencing gate, a differing effective timeout defeats dedup (both run), the flake probe labels FLAKY without ever flipping the verdict, and a plain eval runs its cmd exactly once — so breaking that machinery (e.g. a sweep that re-runs the shared cmd per gate, or a probe that absolves) still reddens the named checks.
violation: Computing the drift set on a re-specified fixture at assertion time returns the gate under test (the count assertions then hold only because the sweep excluded it); any of the pinned counts (1 shared run + 1 probe, 2 runs under differing timeout, 3 failing referencing gates, exactly-once eval) is no longer asserted; or a targeted break of the guarded machinery in a fixture copy (dedup memo removed, flake probe made absolving) leaves the corresponding check green.
